issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to adapt and run a deployment script named build.sh/build.bat (including adding specific Gradle/Docker/Heroku commands), but neither build.sh nor build.bat exists in the template repository. This makes it impossible for students to follow the specified workflow without first creating these files on their own, and the template provides no designated place to implement the required steps.
issues.suggestedFix: Add build.sh and build.bat to the repository root in the template (with TODO placeholders matching the listed steps), or update the problem statement to reference the actual script filename(s) that students should edit and run.

issues.description: The problem statement and Dockerfile template require copying and executing a start.sh script (e.g., "Copy start.sh" and "CMD ./start.sh"), but no start.sh file is present in the provided template repository listing. This blocks students from successfully building/running the Docker image as instructed because the referenced entrypoint script is missing.
issues.suggestedFix: Include a start.sh file in the template repository root that starts the Spring Boot jar (respecting Heroku PORT), or change the instructions and Dockerfile template to run the jar directly (e.g., via ENTRYPOINT/CMD without start.sh).

issues.description: The solution's heroku-app-name.txt contains "H10E01-Containers" (uppercase letters), but Heroku app names must be lowercase and may only contain letters, numbers, and dashes. Using the solution value as-is would fail Heroku commands like "heroku container:release ... -a <app-name>" and confuse students about what to put into heroku-app-name.txt.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a valid lowercase Heroku app name in solution_repository/heroku-app-name.txt (e.g., "h10e01-containers" or an example placeholder), and optionally add a short note in the problem statement about Heroku app-name constraints.
